transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve gotten into this habit of making myself throw up after I eat, and I can’t seem to stop doing it even though I know it’s not right. It's really embarrassing to admit, but I feel like I need some help to stop.
When you do this, are you eating an unusually large amount of food in a short time and feeling out of control while eating, or are you vomiting after more normal-sized meals?

It's mostly after I eat huge amounts of food really fast when I get home from a stressful shift, like plowing through half a pizza and chips in twenty minutes. It feels like a switch flips and I completely lose control, even though my brain is screaming at me to stop. Sometimes I'll also throw up after greasy food truck lunches at work, too.
How often do these binge-eating episodes and self-induced vomiting happen, and for about how many months has this been going on?

This has been going on for about five months now, ever since I took on the lead tech role at my shop. It happens pretty much every week, where I'll binge on several nights when I get home and force myself to throw up at least a couple of times a week.
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you feel about yourself? Are you making yourself vomit mainly to prevent weight gain or because you feel very upset about your body shape?

My weight and shape pretty much dictate how I feel about myself—if my coveralls look tight next to the younger techs at the shop, I feel like a total failure. I throw up because of both, honestly; I panic if the scale creeps up even half a pound, and I'm so upset about my body shape that I do it so the weight won't "stick."

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control, followed by recurrent self-induced vomiting to prevent weight gain, occurring at least weekly for about five months. Self-evaluation is excessively influenced by body weight and shape. This pattern is most consistent with bulimia nervosa.
